captive_summary: No public source describes a power-generation design for this project. Multiple 2023-2026 news items (Reuters, TanzaniaInvest, African Energy, allAfrica) confirm the project is still at the negotiation/HGA stage, not at a published-design stage, which is consistent with no power-system details being public yet.

captive_summary: This is an explicit, well-documented 'LNG-to-power' project: the FSU (Vasant) + FRU (Torman, a 28,000 cbm Jiangnan-built, BV-classed regasification barge delivered ~Nov 2020, operated by Reganosa) regasifies LNG and delivers it into Ghana's national grid / GNPC's industrial and power customers via an ~8km onshore pipeline — the direction test points to NOT captive (gas flows OUT to external power plants, e.g. the nearby VRA-owned Tema Thermal Power Complex). However, per the FSRU-onboard convention this direction-test finding does not by itself answer the question — no public source describes the FSU/FRU's own power supply (shore power vs onboard generation, and if onboard, its fuel), so the verdict stays INSUFFICIENT rather than NO pending that specific finding.
confirmed_how: LNG Prime ("Tema LNG FRU heading towards Ghana", 2020) and Bureau Veritas classification coverage (LNG Prime, 2021) identify the FRU as 'Torman FRU', 94.90m, 28,000 cbm, two TGE type-C tanks, five modular regas modules, built by Jiangnan Shipyard, ~1.7-2 mtpa capacity. LNG Prime's Reganosa contract article and Offshore Energy's 'Reganosa to run LNG-to-power project in Ghana' both frame the whole project as an LNG-to-power scheme delivering gas 'into the national grid' of Ghana. None of these, nor the NS Energy project profile, describe the FRU/FSU's own hotel-load power source.
